author: nonretail_writer
central_thesis: Two shocks are hitting at once: a 7.5% January CPI that has pulled the Fed toward a faster March lift-off (two-year at 1.50%, up 59 bps over 20 observations; bear-flattening curve with 10Y−2Y at +42 bps) and White House warnings that Russia could invade Ukraine within the week (VIX 27.36, Brent 94.44 USD/bbl, S&P 500 down 1.90% on Friday). The edition therefore favours energy, defense, gold miners and short-duration cash-flow assets over long-duration growth and semiconductors, keeps China and Poland Mixed because policy support (PBOC easing, a hawkish NBP and a firm zloty) offsets property and frontline risk, and changes the call on a verifiable Russian de-escalation combined with a softer next inflation print.
sources_policy: Evidence is limited to the frozen 2022-02-14 feed (read through tools/digest.py, topic listings and --grep) and the 2022-02-14 market card (tools/showcard.py). The cutoff is 00:00:00 UTC on 14 February 2022; every cited item is inside its feed window, and none of the IDs in exclusions/2022-02-14.json is cited. No other date's feed, card, spec, draft or note, no specs/, retail_drafts/, notes/retail_* or audit/independent_* file, and no web source was used. One process incident: the first batch of topic listings was written to a shared scratch path, and another writer's process overwrote some of those files, so one listing (the 2022-02-01 sectors topic) was briefly displayed. It was discarded on detection, nothing from it was used, and every listing relied on was then regenerated in a date-specific scratch folder and checked against own-date item counts. Card values are quoted exactly with Yahoo Finance / US Treasury / crypto daily-close tags. Japanese equities use their 2022-02-10 session because Tokyo was closed on 11 February. No numeric spot-FX level or return is quoted; the zloty is described only by direction from dated Bankier reports, and the dollar only through the DXY index. Each citation ID is used at most twice (263 distinct IDs), so the merged report stays within the four-use cap. Polish companies appear only in the PL block, Underowned and nowhere in the Sector Deep Dive. Final verifier run (tools/verify.py --nonretail 2022-02-14): PASS, 8,981 body words, 0 FAIL, 0 WARN, so no warning needed justification. Every cited sentence was then re-read against its headline wording, outlet, timestamp and outcome-versus-preview status.
